content:
Maria Chen: Heads up — apac1 p99 token latency jumped ~600ms since 02:15 UTC after runtime rollout. Traces show continuous-batcher queueing increased. @Jun can you confirm?

Jun Park: looking now. I see batcher latency up, and KV cache hit rate dropped from 98% -> 73% around 02:14. Possibly regression in batching commit that changed prefetching/prefork behavior.

Alex Rivera: I'm seeing a correlated spike in na-east edge too, looks like autoscale not draining quickly. Replaying load against model gpt-open-1b reproduces the queueing locally.

Priya Desai: adding oncall-bot to thread
oncall-bot: Incident created INC-20260318-041. Pager duty triggered.

Jun Park: root cause appears to be continuous-batcher tweak in runtime 2026.03.17-rc3 that changed batch window logic + disabled a small KV cache pre-warm. More misses -> extra backend RPCs -> higher tail latency.

Maria Chen: Can we revert that runtime flag or roll back the change? We need a fast mitigation.

Alex Rivera: Rolling rollback on apac1 hotpool now:
```bash
./deploy rollback --target apac1 --service runtime --tag 2026.03.16
```

deploy-bot: Started rollback job job-7894. ETA ~7m.

Jun Park: Meanwhile pushing a portion of traffic off apac1 to na-west to reduce peak. Updating routing policy now.

Priya Desai: Command to reroute (applied via route-service):
```json
{"route_policy":"region-preference","preferred":"na-west","weight_shift":0.25}
```

Sam O'Neill: Suggest enabling KV cache soft-ttl fallback to reduce backend churn while rollback is in progress. I can flip the config on config-service for apac1 edges.

Maria Chen: Go for it Sam, do it and post what you changed.

Sam O'Neill: Flipped soft-ttl to 60s: 
```yaml
kvcache:
  soft_ttl_seconds: 60
  prewarm_enabled: true
```
Applied to apac1. Observability: cache hit rate trending up, backend RPCs dropping.

Jun Park: Rollback completed on apac1 hotpool, runtime tag now 2026.03.16. All nodes report healthy.

deploy-bot: Rollback job job-7894 succeeded.

Maria Chen: Monitoring — p99 back to baseline in ~6m after both rollback + kvcache tweak. Good work. We'll keep reroute in place for 30m to smooth traffic.

Alex Rivera: Logging capacity and cost impact — early numbers show na-west GPU-hours spiked for the mitigation window. I'll capture exact deltas.

Priya Desai: We'll run a tighter canary for the continuous-batcher change next time with KV cache emulation and a reduced batch-window. Also add a healthcheck that monitors kvcache hit-rate delta.

Jun Park: Adding a feature flag for the prefetch behavior so we can toggle without full deploy. Also pinning the batch-window param for canaries.

Maria Chen: Please document the rollback steps in the incident ticket and schedule a short postmortem. Note the cost impact so finance can be notified: reroute + extra replicas = obvious delta. @Alex please add GPU-hour and egress estimates.

Alex Rivera: Will upload a short spreadsheet and the infra metrics to the ticket. Early estimate: ~+12% GPU-hours for na-west and ~+$700 of additional egress for the 45m mitigation window.

Priya Desai: I've created a follow-up task to add an automated alarm on kvcache hit-rate >5% drop in 5m.

Jun Park: Also adding a small test harness that replays realistic KV-cache access patterns during canary.

Maria Chen: Closing incident after monitoring window ends. Thanks for the quick ops. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260318-041 resolved.

Alex Rivera: FYI I uploaded stack traces, traces and flamegraphs to the incident ticket (links included there).

Maria Chen: Thanks team — good catch and quick rollback. We'll iterate on safer canaries and feature flags.
